sections.title: Bottlenecks — Risk & Opportunity
sections.note: dual-readable: every risk is a substitution play

risk.title: Rare-earth permanent magnets
risk.text: Single-source — China controls >90% of global processing, and India imported 60–80% of magnet value from it. Design and homologation requalification for magnet-free motors is slow. Resilience: years.

opp.title: REPM scheme + magnet-free motors
opp.text: The ₹7,280 cr REPM scheme (6,000 MTPA, rare-earth corridors in Odisha/Kerala/AP/TN) and ferrite/SRM motor design (Sona Comstar, Uno Minda) are the domestic capture plays.

risk.title: Li-ion cells & active materials
risk.text: Cathode, anode, electrolyte and separator are overwhelmingly imported; ACC-PLI has commissioned ~1.4 GWh of a 50 GWh target with zero disbursals. Resilience: years.

opp.title: Gigafactories & upstream materials
opp.text: Agratas (Tata), Ola, Reliance, Exide–SVOLT and Amara Raja–Gotion are building cells; the cathode/anode/electrolyte chain is an almost-empty domestic market.

risk.title: Automotive semiconductors
risk.text: MCU/SoC, power (SiC/IGBT), analog and MEMS are near-totally imported; AEC-Q requalification is slow. Resilience: years.

opp.title: ATMP, design & software value
opp.text: CG Power ATMP and Tata Electronics (fab + OSAT, unlisted) build back-end capacity; KPIT and Tata Elxsi capture ECU/ADAS/SDV value without owning a fab.

risk.title: Capital equipment & electrical steel
risk.text: Forging presses, HPDC machines, CNC tools, SMT lines and cell-fab equipment are imported; motor-grade electrical steel is largely imported too. Resilience: months–years.

opp.title: Machine-tool localisation
opp.text: Capital-goods PLI and Indian cell-line/SMT integrators; domestic CRGO/CRNGO expansion (JSW, Tata Steel) is a prerequisite for localising magnet-free motors and chargers. Deepest hidden dependency: imported capital equipment and upstream specialty materials — magnets, cells, electrical steel and semiconductors — sit under every "made-in-India" vehicle. Localising assembly without localising these leaves the highest-value layers imported.

sections.title: Value pools & cost waterfall
sections.note: where value is captured · and which pool leaks to imports

items: Upstream materials & specialty inputs (magnets, cells, electrical steel, semiconductors) capture the highest, most defensible value — and mostly leak to imports.
Electronics & software (ADAS, ECUs, SDV) carry the fastest-rising content-per-vehicle and proprietary margins.
Forging/casting/fastener tiers are globally competitive but capital-heavy and margin-thin — India's strongest export franchise.
OEM assembly is scale-driven; EV OEMs are burning cash to hold share.
Aftermarket (₹99,948 cr) is the most resilient domestic pool, riding the ageing parc.
Uno Minda — broadest value-added content (switches, lighting, alloy wheels, EV systems); ₹19,589 cr FY26.
Samvardhana Motherson — wiring harness + modules at scale; ₹126,104 cr FY26.
Sona Comstar — deepest EV-tech content (motors, controllers, driveline); Denso JVs.
Bharat Forge / Ramkrishna / Sundram Fasteners — export-led forging & fastener margins.
KPIT / Tata Elxsi — software value with no capex.
Rare-earth magnets (60–80% of value).
Li-ion cells & active materials.
Semiconductors (MCU, power, sensors).
Electrical steel.
Capital equipment (presses, CNC, SMT, cell lines).
Collectively these are the bulk of India's ~20–30% import dependence.

digest.h: Snapshot India's auto-component industry turned over ₹6.73 lakh crore in FY25 and flipped a rare $453 mn trade surplus, but that became a ~$200 mn deficit in H1 FY26 as US tariffs stalled exports and China imports jumped. Two-wheelers are the most localised chain; every EV powertrain node hides an import wall. Process & equipment
items: Spine: melting → forging/casting → precision machining → heat treatment → assembly → test/homologation.
Forging presses, HPDC die-casting machines, CNC tools and cell-fab/SMT lines are all imported — the deepest hidden dependency.
EV adds motor winding, power-module assembly, cell electrode coating/formation and pack EOL testing.
Rare-earth permanent magnets — single-source (China >90% of processing). Resilience: years.
Li-ion cells & active materials — ACC-PLI has commissioned ~1.4 GWh of 50 GWh, zero disbursals.
Automotive semiconductors (MCU/SoC, SiC/IGBT, sensors) — near-total import.
Electrical steel and capital equipment (presses, CNC, cell lines).
Upstream materials, cells, magnets and semiconductors capture the highest value — and leak to imports.
Electronics & software carry the fastest-rising content-per-vehicle and proprietary margins.
Forging/casting/fasteners are globally competitive but capital-heavy and margin-thin — the export franchise (Bharat Forge, Ramkrishna, Sundram).
Broadest value-added content stays domestic with Uno Minda and Samvardhana Motherson; deepest EV-tech with Sona Comstar.
Aftermarket (₹99,948 cr) is the most resilient domestic pool, riding the ageing parc.

Correction from the prior run: the PM E-DRIVE e-2W demand incentive now runs to 31 Mar 2028 (S.O. 4424(E), 10 Aug 2026), not 31 Jul 2026; supported-vehicle cap raised to 45,79,120 and scheme outlay to ₹11,900 cr.

Correction from the prior run: the India–US interim deal that would cut auto-part tariffs (~50% → 0–18%, Feb-2026) is still unsigned, but commerce minister Goyal said on 15-Oct-2026 that the first tranche is finalised with legal drafting under way (he had called it “concluded” in substance on 10-Oct-2026; FM Sitharaman had called the talks a “plateau”, 5-Oct-2026; USTR Greer said a deal was “not imminent”, 2-Oct-2026). Indian exports to the US currently face a 10% tariff, with up to 100% risked under the Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act 2026.
REPM scheme (₹7,280 cr, 6,000 MTPA) tenders expected 2026; production ~2 years out.
China eased light-RE magnets to four Indian firms; heavy magnets still restricted.
No NSE/BSE pure-play in rare-earth magnets, cell active materials, automotive semiconductors or electrical steel; nearest exposure is via conglomerates or unlisted arms.
